chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubaydullah al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

We asked him (peace be upon him) about the charity (khums) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the charity of Fatima (peace be upon her). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their charity is for Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.'
ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to receive the charity (khums) of the Prophet and Fatima?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the specific distribution of Sadaqah (alms) from the Prophet Muhammad and Fatima al-Zahra, restricting it to Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes their Sadaqah from the general public's, thereby exempting them from the Zakat paid by others while allowing them to receive it. The narration underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in the economic and spiritual hierarchy of the early Muslim community.
